message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy the B_O_RAILROAD or start an auction.

I own the yellow monopoly with two houses on Ventnor and Marvin. I am checking the game state for house counts.

The game state shows zero houses on every property, contradicting my private note that two houses were placed on Ventnor and Marvin.

The public timeline shows no BUILDINGS_BUILT events for me, so the house placements likely never occurred. My cash of $357 matches the pre-build total before mortgaging, confirming the earlier private notes about building were not reflected in the actual game state.

I will trust the authoritative game state over my private memory. I have $357 and three mortgaged properties, so I can afford the $200 B&O Railroad. The only other unowned railroad is the fourth in the group, which would give me a single $25 rent.

Player two has $974 and brown hotels, making them a dangerous monopolist. Auctioning the railroad would let them bid aggressively for under $200. Buying it outright leaves $157, which is barely enough to build yellow houses at $150 each.

I cannot build three houses on the yellows with only $357. Two houses would cost $300 and leave me with just $57. Buying the railroad for $200 would leave only $157, which is barely enough for one house.

The yellow monopoly is my win condition. Building houses there is far more valuable than a single $25 railroad rent.

Player one has already developed orange properties with two or three houses, making them a dangerous threat.

Player three has cash and partial reds or boardwalk. Blocking player two from completing the railroad set is a major strategic priority. The value of preventing a fourth railroad may outweigh the cost of one yellow house.

Standard Monopoly railroad rent is $25, $50, $100, and $200. Player two would gain $100 per landing on their three existing railroads if they acquire B&O. Chance cards increase the probability of hitting a railroad, so the expected value of blocking them from completing the set needs careful calculation.

Player one's orange properties are extremely dangerous. St. James and Tennessee each have two houses, and New York has three. Their combined rent is $200, $200, and $600 per landing. Player one has only $270 in cash, so they could quickly build more houses if they acquire additional funds.

The yellow monopoly rent schedule is now clear. One house on each property yields $110, $110, and $120. Two houses raise this to $330, $330, and $360. Three houses would generate $800, $800, and $850 per landing. This confirms the plan to spend $300 on two houses and leave $57 in cash.

I have decided not to buy the B&O Railroad. One house on a single yellow is too weak to justify spending $200. Player one has only $270 and will likely bid in an auction to block player two from completing their railroad set. Player three has $754 and could also bid. I am weighing whether starting an auction would let me participate in that bidding.

I can decline the purchase and bid in the subsequent auction. If I win for under $120, that would be a cheap denial of player two's railroad set. Player one or player three might overbid and drain their own cash. I will not spend $200 outright.

I now see that starting an auction risks letting player two acquire the railroad cheaply. I will not spend $200 on it to block them, because building three yellow houses is the true win condition.

I realized that spending $200 on the railroad would leave me with only $157. That is too little to survive a $600 orange rent hit or even a $200 two-house orange hit. I have already mortgaged Park, PA, and Oriental Avenue. If I had to mortgage a yellow property to pay rent, that would block my house-building plans entirely.

I cannot mortgage any yellow properties. The game rules forbid building houses on a color group while any property in that set is mortgaged. All non-yellow properties are already mortgaged, leaving no cash reserves to cover a $600 orange rent hit.

I will start the auction. I may signal interest to inflate the price against player two, then withdraw.

I will not publicly express disinterest in the railroad. That would let player two acquire it cheaply. I will instead signal that I might bid, which should inflate the auction price and allow me to withdraw.
